transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Leah Park (Redwood CSM), John Patel (Silverline Eng Lead), Priya Kumar (Silverline Product), Zoe Li (Silverline Head of Security), Eli Turner (Silverline SRE)

Summary:
Quick QBR-style handoff focusing on usage patterns, rising token costs, reliability incidents last quarter, and alignment on pilot & roadmap for the next 6 weeks. Action items: pricing, stress test, SOC2 packet, pilot kickoff schedule.

Topics covered:
- Current usage and spike windows (batch vs interactive)
- Cost drivers and optimization levers (batching, quantization, KV cache hits)
- Recent reliability incidents and tail-latency causes
- Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs and burst policies
- Compliance/Security checklist (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs)
- Pilot scope and success criteria

Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription has occasional errors):
[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll do a quick runthrough of the numbers then handoff to Carlos for the stress/technical plan.
[00:00:14] John: Yep thanks, Maya. We wanted this to be a combined health + pilot planning, so thanks for setting it up.
[00:00:28] Maya: Great. Leah is on for CSM context, but quick note: recorded for internal notes. If any red flags, flag them.
[00:00:45] Leah: Hi all. We saw 38% month over month growth in inference requests, and cost is creeping. I'll let Carlos show the breakdown.
[00:01:05] Carlos: Cool. So looking at the token-level breakdown, most of the increase is from larger batched jobs between 14:00-18:00 UTC, and an uptick in long-context chats we haven't cached. The KV cache hit rate dropped from around 72% to 58% in early Nov, which increases token regen.
[00:01:30] Priya: Sorry can you say K V cache again? We are not 100% on what that metric means.
[00:01:38] Carlos: Yeah sorry, KV cache - key value cache. It's prefix caching for repeated prompts. Lower hits means more tokens generated per request.
[00:01:52] Eli: That matches our logs; lots of unique session IDs due to a change in session keying last sprint, so we massively reduced reuse. That was my bad, we rolled a fix but some sessions are still sticky.
[00:02:10] John: So is the primary cost driver the fewer cache hits or the sequence length change?
[00:02:18] Carlos: Both. Sequence length increased too — average seq went from 420 tokens to 640 tokens in peak windows. That's roughly +50% token spend. Cache hit drop is multiplicative.
[00:02:35] Maya: Ok, big picture. There are optimization levers: adjust session keying to increase cache hits, adopt prefix caching guidance from our Optimize tool, tune batching windows and use a quantized model for background tasks.
[00:02:51] Priya: For quantization, we are worried about quality and hallucination changes. Do you have data on tradeoffs?
[00:02:59] Carlos: Yes, we ran internal evals on 4-bit and 8-bit profiles. 8-bit gave ~20% cost down with negligible quality delta on our eval prompts; 4-bit had some regression on certain instruction types. We can share the eval deck.
[00:03:20] Zoe: On the security front, we need to confirm KMS integration and whether Redwood stores any customer plaintext logs. Also retention policy and where audit logs land.
[00:03:33] Maya: Good call — we will share the SOC2 + ISO packet and the storage flow diagram. Short answer: hosted mode keeps ephemeral payloads for X hours and audit logs go to a customer-configurable destination with optional KMS envelope encryption. For Private, customers control keys entirely.
[00:03:56] Zoe: When you say ephemeral payloads 'X hours' can you be specific?
[00:04:02] Leah: We usually quote 24 hours by default for debug traces, but you can configure to 0 retention in Private plus send logs to your SIEM.
[00:04:12] Zoe: Ok need that in writing.
[00:04:15] Maya: Absolutely. I'll attach the compliance packet and the retention config doc.
[00:04:22] John: Back to reliability incidents — can you summarize the Nov 3rd tail-latency spike? We saw a 7% user-visible latency increase for about 40 minutes.
[00:04:34] Carlos: Yeah that was a combo of a firmware rollout on a GPU host and an unlucky model auto-redeploy combined with a spike in long-context requests. The routing fallback kicked in but there was a clear cold-KV path that wasn't optimized. We've got a postmortem draft that explains mitigations: pin kernel versions to avoid rolling host-level firmware during heavy windows, and improve the warm pool prefetch for KV caches.
[00:05:00] Eli: Can you share the postmortem? Our ops will need it for our incident review.
[00:05:05] Carlos: I'll drop the postmortem link to the shared board after the call.
[00:05:12] Priya: On canaries and rollouts — we want finer control. Is there a way to do A/B rollback automatically?
[00:05:20] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console supports canary with health checks and automatic rollback based on latency and error thresholds. You can configure the route to fall back to a cheaper variant. Note: automatic fallback to a quantized variant is supported but you must opt-in for quality locking.
[00:05:36] John: Can that fallback be region-aware? We have EU compliance requests and want EU-only fallback.
[00:05:42] Carlos: Routing policy supports region tags. We can pin a route to EU-only and have a EU fallback policy to another EU region.
[00:05:52] Zoe: On Private deployment — if we go with Private in our VPC, is there still a shared control plane? We need to know blast radius and management plane access.
[00:06:02] Maya: For Private you get a control-plane tenant dedicated to your account; networking is customer's. You can opt for an air-gapped package where we ship the runtime and you manage cluster upgrades. In that mode, Redwood does not hold keys.
[00:06:17] Zoe: Good. We'll need a formal attestation doc for that.
[00:06:22] Maya: Noted.
[00:06:25] Leah: Quick health numbers: 99.2% p99 availability last 30 days, but p95 latency slipped from 220ms to 330ms on peaks. Error rate stayed below 0.3%.
[00:06:38] Eli: Does the 99.2% include the time your routing fallback was running?
[00:06:43] Carlos: Yes, that's a platform-wide metric. For their account specifically, we saw 99.6% but a couple of bursts.
[00:06:50] John: Our top business metric is user conversion in chat flows; any latency above ~300ms reduces conversion significantly per our internal funnel. We need to keep p95 under 250ms ideally.
[00:07:03] Maya: Understood. Action: Carlos will propose a configuration to keep p95 <250ms during peak windows — likely Dedicated with reserved burst capacity for peak hours and stricter pre-warming.
[00:07:16] Carlos: The tradeoff is cost. Dedicated reserved capacity reduces tail by about 35% but increases baseline cost. There's also the option of smart-batching and aggressive KV cache tuning to reduce tokens without Dedicated.
[00:07:30] Priya: Can you give a ballpark cost delta for Dedicated? We need that for our finance review.
[00:07:36] Maya: We'll send a formal sheet, but roughly Dedicated committed for their profile is ~1.8x the hosted steady-state but gives predictable latency and capacity. With burst described it might be 2x in peak months. We'll refine.
[00:07:51] John: That's a big jump. Would caching + quantization only get us 50% of that gap?
[00:07:58] Carlos: In our experience, caching + 8-bit quant can get 30-45% cost reduction depending on hit rates. If you fix session keying (Eli owns that), I think you could cut a lot of tail spend.
[00:08:12] Eli: I'll prioritize the session keying fix this sprint.
[00:08:16] Maya: Thanks. Let's scope the pilot: two-week pilot, Dedicated warm pool for peak windows, plus a parallel hosted quantized path for background jobs, and a set of eval prompts to detect quality regressions. Success criteria: p95 < 250ms during peak and token cost per active user down 30% YoY baseline.
[00:08:38] Priya: That sounds reasonable. Also want to measure conversion delta on a 5% sample.
[00:08:44] Maya: Good — include conversion metric.
[00:08:48] Leah: I'll track pilot KPIs in the shared tracker.
[00:08:52] Carlos: On the stress test — I'm proposing a 72-hour continuous run that simulates your real QPS and session distribution; will include long-context mixes and ramp ups. We'll feed logs to their SRE team.
[00:09:05] John: Perfect. Make sure to include a cold-start scenario and a firmware patch mid-run to simulate the Nov 3rd conditions.
[00:09:14] Carlos: Yep, we'll do delta patches. That will help validate fallback logic.
[00:09:18] Zoe: For compliance, what's the SLA if we switch to Dedicated + Private? Is there a separate enterprise SLA?
[00:09:27] Maya: Dedicated has SLA SLAs that are stronger; Private enterprise packages include platform uptime SLAs and a support runway. We'll attach the SLA doc.
[00:09:36] Zoe: We'll review the SLA with legal. Also need to confirm data residency on backups — are backups encrypted with our KMS?
[00:09:44] Maya: In Private, yes — customer keys. Hosted can optionally use customer-managed keys for backups. We'll annotate the doc.
[00:09:53] Priya: Regarding pricing: can we have a usage floor and then an overage model? Our CFO prefers committed capacity with overage rather than pay-as-you-go spikes.
[00:10:03] Maya: That's standard with Dedicated reserved: commit for baseline and then overage rates for bursts; we'll show the exact tiers.
[00:10:10] Leah: Also we'll propose a 30-day rollback clause for pilot if quality regressions exceed thresholds.
[00:10:16] John: Helpful.
[00:10:19] Maya: Quick note on analytics: Console will show token-level breakdowns, per-route latency, and cost per user segments. We'll give a walkthrough in the pilot kickoff.
[00:10:31] Priya: Walkthrough please, our product analyst wants to see per-route dashboards.
[00:10:36] Maya: Agreed. We'll demo Console dashboards.
[00:10:40] Carlos: A few technical clarifications: 1) quantization profiles - we need to validate on your evals; 2) batching windows — we can suggest a 35–50ms batching tradeoff for background jobs; 3) KV cache TTL policy tune — we'll recommend 24hrs sliding window for your session use-case.
[00:10:56] Eli: For the batching windows, are those applied in the client SDK or on the server routing layer?
[00:11:02] Carlos: Batching can be applied at client SDK for best packing or the server runtime does continuous batching; we recommend client-side hints plus server-side continuous batch to hit both.
[00:11:12] John: Okay good.
[00:11:15] (short pause)
[00:11:25] Priya: One more question on rollback — if quantized fallback runs automatically and shows small quality drift, can we set an automatic hold or alert threshold?
[00:11:34] Carlos: Yes, we have quality monitors tied to prompt sets and eval scores; if a regression > X% on critical prompts, it will alert and optionally pause fallback.
[00:11:45] Zoe: What's X?
[00:11:47] Carlos: Typically 3–5% drop in weighted eval score; we'll set the threshold with your team.
[00:11:55] Priya: For the pilot, let's set 4%.
[00:11:59] Carlos: Noted.
[00:12:03] Maya: Ok let's recap decisions so far before we go into the scheduling part.
[00:12:08] (recap begins)
[00:12:10] Maya: 1) Pilot scope: 2-week pilot with Dedicated warm pool for peaks + hosted quantized background path. 2) Success: p95 < 250ms and token cost down ~30%; measure conversion. 3) Action items: pricing, stress test, SOC2 docs, session key fix. 4) Next: schedule pilot kickoff next Tue.
[00:12:32] John: Sounds good. 5) We'll provide traffic profile and CSV.
[00:12:36] Eli: Yep I'll send by Friday.
[00:12:39] Maya: Great.
[00:12:42] (--- meeting moves to scheduling and logistics ---)
[00:12:50] Leah: For the pilot kickoff, propose Mon/Tue next week window; prefer Tue 14:00 UTC.
[00:12:58] Priya: Tue 14:00 works for product and analytics.
[00:13:02] Zoe: Works for security too.
[00:13:05] Maya: I'll set the calendar.
[00:13:08] Carlos: On the 72-hour stress run — tentative start next Friday so we can align with Eli's session key fix.
[00:13:15] Eli: I'll try to push fix earlier in the week so we have a stable baseline.
[00:13:19] John: Any open blockers for pilot other than pricing and compliance docs?
[00:13:25] Zoe: SOC2 packet and the Private air-gapped attestation.
[00:13:29] Maya: We'll share both by EOD Thursday.
[00:13:33] Leah: I'll also share a pilot tracker and invite CS stakeholders.
[00:13:37] Maya: Anything else?
[00:13:40] (brief silence)
[00:13:44] Priya: Not from product.
[00:13:46] Eli: No.
[00:13:48] Zoe: No.
[00:13:50] Maya: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the 1-pager and schedule.
[00:13:56] John: Thanks, talk soon.
[00:13:59] Maya: Bye everyone.
